summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease, prior CABG, diabetes, and hypertension was readmitted within 24 hours of discharge due to persistent left shoulder pain, constipation, and abdominal discomfort. She had recently fallen and sustained a musculoskeletal injury when her arm was grabbed. Serial troponins were negative, with no EKG changes, ruling out acute cardiac injury. Pain was reproducible on exam, supporting a musculoskeletal origin. Constipation was managed with bowel regimen adjustments. She remained stable on telemetry, continued her baseline cardiac and diabetes medications, and was discharged home with a short-term pain prescription and follow-up appointments in primary care and cardiology, including a scheduled stress test.
